sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Strategy of the Republic of Croatia to 2040 with a View to 2070
sources.organization: Croatian Parliament; Government of the Republic of Croatia
sources.temporal_coverage: Government strategy adopted in 2020; reports historical sector impacts and RCP4.5 projections for 2011–2040 and 2041–2070, with an outlook to 2070.
sources.methodology: Government strategy blending climate observations, cited damage estimates, projections and sector assessments.
sources.limitations: Historical estimates cite studies; projections use older models and scenario assumptions.

sources.title: Disaster Risk Assessment for the Republic of Croatia
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Croatia; Directorate of Civil Protection, Ministry of the Interior
sources.temporal_coverage: National disaster-risk assessment dated March 2024; registered county damages cover 2010–2021 and declared natural disasters 2014–2022.
sources.methodology: Government assessment combines hazard scenarios, county vulnerability indicators, recorded losses and civil-protection readiness measures.
sources.limitations: Loss figures aggregate declared disasters and hazards; they do not attribute damages to climate change.

sources.title: Preliminary Flood Risk Assessment 2024
sources.organization: Hrvatske vode (Croatian Waters), national water-management authority
sources.temporal_coverage: The 2024 preliminary assessment uses information through 2023 to identify potentially significant flood-risk areas for the 2028–2033 basin-plan cycle.
sources.methodology: State water authority summarizes mapped potentially significant flood-risk areas and basin population exposure.
sources.limitations: Potential exposure zones are not climate-attributed losses; mapping and management plans are planned for 2028–2033.

sources.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Croatia 2026
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Economic survey published 30 January 2026; climate event-loss series covers 1980–2023 and includes reported 2024 events and current policy status.
sources.methodology: OECD country survey reviews reported event losses, subnational exposure and adaptation policy.
sources.limitations: The survey cites underlying EEA and EIB material; figures are not independently recalculated here.

claims.locator: Sections 1.1 and 1.2, climate security and migration framing
claims.paraphrase: The Strategy frames climate change as a Croatian security threat and says climate-related relocation may indirectly destabilize society, while noting migration is multi-causal.
affected_groups: people relocating because of climate impacts
institutions: Government of the Republic of Croatia
claims.limitations: Strategic framing, not evidence of Croatian climate-related displacement or violent incidents.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The Strategy explicitly links adverse climate effects to security, forced relocation and possible societal destabilization, while identifying infrastructure and socioeconomic dysfunction as co-causes.

claims.paraphrase: RCP4.5 projects 5–10% summer/autumn precipitation reductions in southern Lika and southern Dalmatia for 2011–2040, with more drought periods.
claims.limitations: Regional model projections, not observed trends.

claims.paraphrase: The Strategy reports earlier, shorter growing seasons and lower yields in Slavonia and Dalmatia; Dalmatian fruit, olive and grape growers face heat and drought stress.
claims.limitations: Source-era sector assessment; no household disaggregation.

claims.locator: Section 4.2, agriculture vulnerability and drought damage
claims.paraphrase: Summer drought was the largest single cause of agricultural climate-variability damage in 1980–2014; reported 2013–2016 loss totaled HRK 3 billion.
claims.limitations: Strategy-cited estimate; historic loss, not a current figure.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 14–15, county social and economic vulnerability factors
claims.paraphrase: County social-vulnerability indicators include age, income inequality, disability, household size and literacy; economic indicators include poverty risk, unemployment, fiscal balance and county GDP.
claims.limitations: These are assessment indicators, not individual or household vulnerability findings.

claims.locator: PDF p. 20, Table 8, registered damages by hazard, 2010–2021
claims.paraphrase: Registered 2010–2021 disaster damages totaled EUR 3.318 billion; drought accounted for EUR 1.095 billion, floods EUR 539 million and fires EUR 249 million.
claims.limitations: Declared-disaster registry values; damages are not attributed to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF p. 21, Table 9, total reported damages by county, 2010–2021
claims.paraphrase: Reported disaster losses were highest in Primorje-Gorski Kotar (EUR 471 million), Osijek-Baranja (EUR 458 million), Virovitica-Podravina (EUR 448 million) and Vukovar-Srijem (EUR 324 million).
claims.limitations: Mixed-hazard registry totals do not isolate climate events or social-group impacts.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 15–16 and 27–28, county vulnerability and civil-protection readiness measures
claims.paraphrase: The assessment scores county readiness using fire, Red Cross, mountain-rescue, association and company forces; it also tracks local risk assessments and civil-protection action plans.
claims.limitations: Readiness indicators and plans are not measured emergency-response outcomes.

claims.locator: Web page, 2024 assessment summary, results of analyses and comparison with 2018
claims.paraphrase: The 2024 screening identifies 2,951 potentially significant flood-risk areas in the Danube basin (68% of area; 2.37 million residents/91%) and 1,107 in the Adriatic basin (59%; 1.09 million/86%); mapped area grew about 5% nationally since 2018.
affected_groups: residents in potentially significant flood-risk areas
claims.limitations: Potential flood exposure, not climate-attributed losses; percentages use each basin's land and population.

claims.locator: Section 3.6, climate-related extreme-event losses and flood exposure
claims.paraphrase: OECD reports 910 fatalities and EUR 4.1 billion losses from climate-related extreme events (1980–2023); flood risk covers 15% of non-coastal territory, including Zagreb and Rijeka.
claims.limitations: Survey cites underlying EEA/EIB data; flood percentage excludes coastal zones.

claims.paraphrase: OECD identifies low-lying islands and river deltas as vulnerable to sea-level rise, coastal floods and salinisation; 2024 brought heavy-rain floods, record March rain, storms and widespread summer heatwaves.
claims.limitations: The report gives no island- or delta-level population estimates.

claims.locator: Section 3.6, urban heat projections and Zagreb green infrastructure
claims.paraphrase: OECD says Zadar and Rijeka are projected to see the strongest city temperature increases; Zagreb's post-2020 earthquake rebuilding incorporated green infrastructure that can reduce heat and urban-flood risks.
claims.scenario: The inspected survey does not specify the projection period or model scenario.
claims.limitations: City projections have no stated period here; green infrastructure benefits are not an evaluated impact estimate.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the national adaptation strategy, 2024 disaster-risk assessment, 2024 flood-risk assessment and OECD survey; located named regions, cities, basins and counties, but little household-level outcome evidence.

search_audit.query: Croatia climate change security threat migration climate migrants conflict violence official strategy
search_audit.outcome: The official strategy explicitly frames climate change as a security risk and describes a possible climate-migration/social-destabilization pathway, while stating migration is multi-causal; no domestic violent-conflict case was evidenced.

search_audit.query: Croatia conflict violence insecurity war legacy disruption climate adaptation civil protection
search_audit.outcome: Official mine-action text documents residual social, economic, ecological and security effects of the 1990s war, but reviewed sources did not link current conflict or insecurity to interrupted climate adaptation or response.

search_audit.query: Croatia county disaster response capacity civil protection local climate adaptation plans flood preparedness
search_audit.outcome: The national assessment scores county and local civil-protection readiness; OECD describes Zagreb green infrastructure and the Commission records subnational adaptation plans, programme gaps and co-financing.

gaps: HRV is absent from EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json and no countries/HRV baseline directory was present, so there was no prior Croatia dossier to extend.

The 2020 strategy provides an explicit general security/migration framing, but inspected primary sources did not establish a Croatia-specific climate-to-violent-conflict case or show conflict disrupting adaptation.
County loss totals combine hazards and are not climate-attributed; county vulnerability indices use aggregate indicators rather than household-level disaggregation.
The Commission's 2023 adaptation-progress assessment was inspected but is not allocated as a source or claim here because its shared regional URL budget is used by another country record.
The official 2024 Biennial Transparency Report PDF could not be inspected because of reader-size limits; its metadata/search listing was not used to support claims.
